attributes.title: Level 3

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓Did you explore the animation assets and see how different frame intervals affect the animation?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What do you notice about the animation assets in My Assets?

❓ What happens when you adjust the frame interval of an animation asset?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out the ninja that animation assets are made up of multiple pixel art frames. The animation cycles through each frame at the rate determined by the frame interval. The ninja can adjust the frame interval to speed up the animation (using a smaller number) or slow it down (using a larger number).
steps.instructions:
Begin the project by exploring the assets in My Assets. 


Click the Assets menu along the top of the screen, and notice the images, tiles, animations, and tilemap stored in My Assets. 


Open the animation assets, which have an animation icon on the bottom left of the asset. Notice the different frames on the right side. Tinker with the frame interval value, and click Play Animation Preview to see how it affects the animation.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you type assets, a dot operator, and the asset type, followed by the name of the asset inside 2 backticks `` in the tilemap parameter?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What function should be used to display a tilemap on screen?

❓ Where should the name of the tilemap be typed in the setCurrentTilemap function?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to check the documentation if they need help displaying a tilemap on screen.
steps.instructions:
Set a tilemap to appear on screen!


Return to the JavaScript editor, then add a // project set up comment at the top. Display the level1 tilemap asset underneath. 


Click ▶ to see the tilemap appear on the screen!

steps.hints: ❓Did you edit the vx and vy parameters of the moveSprite function so the Player sprite can only move horizontally?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Where can you find the coordinates of a specific tile in the tilemap editor?

❓  Why should the Player sprite only be able to move horizontally on a 2D platformer tilemap?

 

Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that they can use their cursor to hover over a specific tile, then find its coordinates in the bottom left corner of the tilemap editor.

💡 Point out to the ninja that in a 2D tilemap, the user’s perspective is from the side (as opposed to a top-down tilemap, where the user’s perspective is from above). Because the user looks on from the side, velocity and acceleration is needed to simulate gravity in the project and allow the sprite to jump up on the tilemap.

💡 Encourage the ninja to use documentation if they need assistance setting the Player sprite’s image, placing it on the tilemap, or setting the camera to follow it.
steps.instructions:
Add a Player sprite to the project!


Add a // sprite set up comment, then add code to create a Player sprite, set the sprite’s image to the dustMite asset, and place the sprite on the left side of the tilemap. 


Set the Player sprite to move around the tilemap with direction buttons. Since this is a 2D platformer project, the Player sprite should only be able to move horizontally (right and left) on the tilemap.


Then, set the Player sprite to stay in screen, and set the camera to follow the Player sprite.  


Click ▶ to test the Player sprite’s movement.

steps.hints: ❓Did you set the acceleration (ay) and velocity (vy) in the correct places in your program?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why does the Player sprite’s y-acceleration need to be set?

❓ What happens when the A button is pressed? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that y-acceleration adds “gravity” to the project. When the A button is pressed, the Player sprite will “jump up”, since its y-velocity is set to a negative value. After the sprite jumps up, it will be pulled down to the tilemap platform, due to its positive y-acceleration value.
steps.instructions:
Make the Player sprite jump when the A button is pressed!


Under the Player sprite code, use the Player sprite name and a dot operator to set its y-acceleration (ay) to 500 to “pull” the Player sprite down to the ground, like gravity.


Then, add a // game events comment and an A button pressed event to make the Player sprite jump, using the Player sprite name and a dot operator to set its y-velocity (vy) value to -200.


Click ▶ and test the Player sprite jumping mechanics.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use the documentation for help with creating and exporting a new sprite kind from the SpriteKind namespace?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How do you create a new SpriteKind in the JavaScript editor?

❓ Where might the Fan sprites be placed on the tilemap?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Encourage the ninja to use documentation if they need assistance creating a Fan SpriteKind.

💡 Encourage the ninja to open the tilemap asset to identify coordinates between the platform wall tiles and the ring tiles, to place the Fan sprites at.
steps.instructions:
Add the Fan sprites to the project!


The fan sprite is made up of 2 image assets: the fanBlades and the airImage. Create 2 sprites under the Player sprite code, using the matching image assets.


Create a new sprite kind named Fan at the top of the code, then update the sprite kind parameter for both sprites.


Place the Fan sprites in the middle of the tilemap, to the right of the platform wall tiles and to the left of the ring tiles. Tinker with the coordinates in the placeOnTile function until the Fan sprites are placed after the platform wall tiles and before the gold ring tiles. 


Click ▶ to view the location of the fan sprites, then edit the location coordinates as needed.

steps.hints: ❓Did you set the Player sprite’s z-property to 3 so it appears in front of the Fan sprites?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What happens when a sprite’s z-property is set?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that a sprite’s z-property determines the order in which it is drawn to the screen. The higher the z value, the closer to the user the sprite appears.
steps.instructions:
Oh no! The Player sprite appears behind the Fan sprite! 


Under the Player sprite code, use the Player sprite name and a dot operator to set the z-property (z) value to 3.


Click ▶ and move the Player sprite to test that it appears in front of the Fan sprites.

steps.hints: ❓Did you update the loop parameter in both runImageAnimation functions so that the sprite animations continuously loop?
steps.instructions:
Animate the Player and Fan sprites on the tilemap!


Add a // sprite animation comment, then open Animation and drag [animate (mySprite) frames (frames) interval (ms) (500) loop (loop)] underneath.


Use the Player sprite’s name in the sprite parameter. Then, update the frames parameter by deleting the brackets [ ] and typing assets, a dot operator and animation, then typing the dustAnim asset name inside 2 backticks ``. Change the frameInterval parameter to set how quickly the animation plays, and set the loop parameter to true.


Copy and paste the runImageAnimation function on the next line, and update the parameters for the Fan sprite using the airAnim asset.


Click ▶ to see the animated sprites on the tilemap, and adjust the interval parameter if needed!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the location variable from the onOverlapTile event to set the location of the collectedRing tile ?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What happens when the Player sprite overlaps a goldRing tile?

❓ Why might the goldRing tile be replaced with a collectedRing tile, once overlapped by the Player sprite?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 When the Player sprite overlaps a goldRing tile, a collectedRing tile is set at the tile location and the score is changed by 1. 

💡 Point out to the ninja that the score will increase for the amount of time the Player sprite overlaps the goldRing tile. As a result, this may cause the score to increase by varying values on each overlap. By replacing the tile and ending the overlap event, this removes this possibility and offers a visual representation of the overlap on screen.
steps.instructions:
Change the score when the Player sprite overlaps a goldRing tile!


Open Scene and drag [run code on (sprite) of kind (kind) overlaps (tile) at (location)] under // game events.


Use the default values for the kind and handler parameters. Set the tile parameter to the goldRing tile asset.


Open Scene and drag [set (tile) at (loc)] inside the onOverlapTile event. Update the location parameter by typing location, then set the tile parameter to the collectedRing tile asset.


Set the score to 0 underneath // project set up and change the score by 1 inside the onOverlapTile event.


Click ▶ to test out the goldRing tile overlap event.

steps.hints: ❓Did you add a moveSprite function to the event, and update the vx and vy parameters so the Player sprite cannot be controlled by the direction buttons after overlapping the Fan sprite?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What might the Player sprite’s x-velocity be set to so that it blows in the direction of the goldRing tiles?

❓ How do you stop the direction buttons from moving the Player sprite?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that a positive x-velocity value will blow the Player sprite towards the right of the screen, and a negative value will blow the Player sprite towards the left. Using a larger number will increase the fan’s strength.

💡 Prompt the ninja to consider what the vx and vy parameters should be set to in the moveSprite function to stop the direction buttons from moving the Player sprite. Both values should be set to 0 so that the Player sprite does not move.

💡 Remind the ninja to use the sprite parameter from the onOverlap event in their vx and moveSprite code.
steps.instructions:
Make the Fan sprite blow the Player sprite to grab the gold rings!


Create an onOverlap event with the Player and Fan sprite kinds under // game events. 


Inside the event, stop the direction buttons from moving the Player sprite, then change its x-velocity (vx) so the Player sprite blows in the direction of the goldRing tiles. Tinker with the vx value to make the fan strength stronger or weaker. 


Click ▶ to see the Player sprite “fly” across the rest of the tilemap once it overlaps the Fan sprite.

steps.hints: ❓Did you turn the walls on if you added new platform tiles?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Where might you add additional platform or ring tiles on the tilemap?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that platform and ring tiles should be placed strategically on the tilemap, if added. The platform tiles should be placed to the left of the Fan sprites (with walls turned on) and ring tiles should be placed high enough, so that the Player sprite needs to jump up to reach them.
steps.instructions:
Edit the tilemap to adjust the game difficulty.


Click the Assets menu and open the tilemap asset. Add or move the platform and ring tiles to make the game easier or more difficult. 


Click ▶ to test out the difficulty of this project.

steps.hints: ❓Did you  use + to concatenate the info.score() variable with a string to tell the user how many rings they collected?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What code should be used to set the flagTile asset as the tile argument in the onOverlapTile function?

❓ What symbol should be used to concatenate the score variable with a string in the splash function?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that when calling an asset in their code, they need to type assets, a dot operator, the asset type, and the name of the asset inside 2 backticks ``. 

💡 Encourage the ninja to use documentation if they need assistance concatenating the score variable with a string in the splash function.
steps.instructions:
End the game when the Player sprite overlaps the flag tile!


Create a new onOverlapTile event under // game events. Set the tile parameter to the flagTile asset.


Inside the event, add a splash screen that tells the user the number of rings collected.  Concatenate the score with a string to tell the user how many rings they collected.


Add code to reset the game after the splash screen.


Click ▶ to test the game ending code.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use new image assets for the dialog frame and cursor?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What images might be used for the dialog frame and cursor?

❓ What instructions might be shared with the user at the beginning of the project?


Sensei Pro Tip:


💡 Encourage the ninja to use the marquee tool in the paint editor to resize the cursor image.
steps.instructions:
Add instructions to the beginning of the project!


Below // project set up, set the dialog frame and dialog cursor images. Then create a dialog box to share instructions for the project with the user.


Click ▶ to play the completed project!

subgroups.title: Dust Mite Adventure
subgroups.introduction: Create a project that uses physics to change how a sprite moves around a 2D platformer tilemap.

validationItems.text: Display a tilemap asset on screen.
Create a Player sprite using an image asset and place the sprite on a specific tilemap location. Set the sprite to stay in screen and for the camera to follow it.
Set the Player sprite’s physics so that it jumps up when the A button is pressed, then is pulled down to the ground.
Animate the Player and Fan sprites.
Change the tile when the Player sprite overlaps a goldRing tile.
Set the Player sprite to move on its own after overlapping with Fan sprites.
Set the project to reset once the Player sprite reaches a flag tile.
Use image assets in the dialog frame and cursor image functions.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 3 of Brown Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about using physics and Boolean values to control game conditions in 2D platform tilemap projects. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 3:

badges.title: Taking Control
badges.description: Control the way sprites move and appear on screen in a 2D tilemap project in JavaScript.

badges.title: Gravity of the Situation
badges.description: Use physics to control a sprite’s velocity and acceleration in a 2D tilemap project in JavaScript.

badges.title: Checkin’ it Twice
badges.description: Check for a specific tile image at a specific tilemap location.

badges.title: While You’re At It…
badges.description: Use a while loop to make something happen while a certain condition is true.

badges.title: And the Winner Is…
badges.description: Create a function that uses Boolean operators and values to determine which sprite image to use.

badges.title: Well-Rounded Character
badges.description: Edit an image asset to create multiple versions of an image that faces different directions.
